subject: Helix Analytics renewal — private offer acceptance, capacity canary, and tax split
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom@helixanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:13:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + uplift — need private offer wording for acceptance window

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the call earlier. Helix is prepared to move forward with the private offer but the finance team asked for two clarifications before we sign: 1) a short acceptance window (we prefer 30 days) with a canary capacity release for the first 60 days so we can validate traffic and 2) a clear split for VAT and tax invoicing between the US entity and our EU subsidiary (we operate cross-border).

I've attached the draft PO and a proposed commit schedule for reference. Can Redwood confirm we can codify the canary capacity (20% of committed GPUs for the first 60 days) and provide a suggested DocuSign workflow so our legal/procurement can circulate? Also flag any lead time for regional marketplace approvals if we route via AWS Marketplace private offer.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our goal is to have this signed before the end of September.

Best,
Tom Alvarez
Director, Procurement
Helix Analytics

Attachments: Helix_Private_Offer_Draft_2026-09-14.pdf (pdf), Helix_PO_Commit_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift — need private offer wording for acceptance window

Hi Tom — thanks, and great to hear Helix wants to proceed. High-level quick answers below; we'll follow with internal owners and a redline by EOD tomorrow.

- Acceptance window: 30 days is fine; we'll mark the private offer to expire in 30 days from issuance.
- Canary capacity: we can set a staged activation schedule in the private offer. 20% for first 60 days then ramp to 100% over an additional 30 days is a reasonable pattern.
- Tax split: Kimberly will confirm the marketplace invoicing path — AWS Marketplace supports consolidated invoicing with tax allocation, but for cross-border splits we'll typically need a separate customer billing contact and a manual invoice for the EU entity.
- DocuSign flow: we generally create the DocuSign envelope after Marketplace acceptance; Marissa will propose the signer set.

Looping in Kimberly and Marissa to confirm the ops/legal checklist and any lead time for marketplace acceptance. Tom, what signatory cadence does your legal team prefer (single signer + PO or two-step: PO -> executive)?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Folks — quick ops notes from marketplace/legal: 

1) AWS Private Offer path: allow 7–10 business days for Marketplace review after we submit the private offer draft; if Helix needs faster, we can request expedited review but it is not guaranteed.
2) Canary capacity: we will encode the staged activation into the private-offer metadata (activation_date + staged_percent) and create a canary routing policy on our side. Ops would like the 20% initial capacity to be pinned to a single region (us-west-2) for monitoring. If Helix needs multi-region canary, call it out now.
3) Tax/invoicing: for the EU split, we will need the EU billing entity's VAT number and a billing contact. We will generate two invoices post-acceptance (one via marketplace invoice flow, one manual B2B invoice) so taxes land in the right place.

I will prepare the private-offer redline and a minimal acceptance checklist: acceptance window, activation schedule, region pin for canary, signer set, billing entity info. Targeting draft for Rachel to share with Helix by EOD 16 Sep.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
